extracted.subtask_description: Table of contents and headings from the Reuters General Style Guide covering editorial, legal and ethical standards (accuracy, defamation, privacy, investment disclosure, handling stringers, dangerous situations, etc.) for producing news content.

rubrics_metrics.name: General Tips
rubrics_metrics.description: General Tips (umbrella heading for practical editorial guidance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Accuracy (guideline heading emphasising factual correctness in reporting).

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance
rubrics_metrics.description: Balance (guideline heading emphasising impartiality and giving fair representation to relevant perspectives).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of quotes
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of quotes (guidance on when and how to quote sources directly).

rubrics_metrics.description: Unnamed sources (rules/guidance on use of anonymous or unattributed sources).

rubrics_metrics.description: Graphic details, obscenities and blasphemy (Attention Editor item flagging potentially offensive or legally sensitive content).

rubrics_metrics.description: Hiring stringers (guidance/procedures for engaging freelance/local reporters).

rubrics_metrics.description: Handling material from stringers (guidance on verifying and using content from stringers).

rubrics_metrics.description: Threats, Claims of Responsibility and Hostage-Taking (guidance on reporting and handling such claims safely and ethically).

rubrics_metrics.description: When to file a report (criteria/triggers for reporting incidents involving staff).

rubrics_metrics.name: Defamation
rubrics_metrics.description: Defamation (legal guidance covering what constitutes defamation and how to avoid it).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes 'What is defamation?', 'What is a defamatory statement?', 'Defamation and images', 'Who may sue?', 'Elements of action' and common defences.

rubrics_metrics.name: What is defamation?
rubrics_metrics.description: What is defamation? (explanatory heading defining the concept).

rubrics_metrics.name: What is a defamatory statement?
rubrics_metrics.description: What is a defamatory statement? (guidance on features that make a statement defamatory).

rubrics_metrics.name: Defamation and images
rubrics_metrics.description: Defamation and images (guidance relating to images that may be defamatory).

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may sue?
rubrics_metrics.description: Who may sue? (guidance on which persons or entities can bring defamation actions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Elements of action
rubrics_metrics.description: Elements of action (the component elements required for a defamation claim).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sub-elements listed: Element 1 - Is it defamatory?; Element 2 - Does the statement identify the claimant?; Element 3 - Has the statement been published?

rubrics_metrics.name: Element 1 - Is it defamatory?
rubrics_metrics.description: Element 1 - Is it defamatory? (assessment of whether material lowers a person's reputation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Element 2 - Does the statement identify the claimant?
rubrics_metrics.description: Element 2 - Does the statement identify the claimant? (assessment of identification).

rubrics_metrics.name: Element 3 - Has the statement been published?
rubrics_metrics.description: Element 3 - Has the statement been published? (publication element of defamation).

rubrics_metrics.description: Common defences to a defamation action (umbrella for legal defences).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes 'Truth/justification', 'Fair comment', 'Absolute privilege', 'Statutory qualified privilege', 'Common-law qualified privilege'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defences 1 - Truth/justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Defences 1 - Truth/justification (the defence that a statement is true).

rubrics_metrics.name: Defences 2 - Fair comment
rubrics_metrics.description: Defences 2 - Fair comment (defence for opinions on matters of public interest).

rubrics_metrics.name: Defences 3 - Absolute privilege
rubrics_metrics.description: Defences 3 - Absolute privilege (complete legal immunity in specific contexts).

rubrics_metrics.name: Defences 4 - Statutory qualified privilege
rubrics_metrics.description: Defences 4 - Statutory qualified privilege (statutory protections for certain publications).

rubrics_metrics.name: Defences 5 - Common-law qualified privilege
rubrics_metrics.description: Defences 5 - Common-law qualified privilege (common-law protections subject to conditions).

rubrics_metrics.description: Contempt and court reporting restrictions (rules on what can be reported about ongoing legal proceedings).

rubrics_metrics.description: Copyright and stringers (how copyright interacts with material supplied by freelancers/stringers).
